sentence: Alpha blockers, also called alpha-adrenoreceptor antagonists, are medicines that relax muscle; tamsulosin is used to relax the muscle around the bladder and prostate in an enlarged prostate.
In an enlarged prostate, tamsulosin relaxes the muscle around the bladder and prostate gland, which makes it easier to pee.
Taking more than one alpha blocker, or combining one with medicines for high blood pressure, can lower blood pressure too much.
Orthostatic hypotension, low blood pressure causing dizziness on standing, is listed by the NHS as a reason tamsulosin is not suitable.
Dizziness or light-headedness, especially on standing.
An allergic reaction to one alpha blocker, such as alfuzosin, doxazosin, prazosin or terazosin, is a reason the NHS lists against tamsulosin.
Alfuzosin, doxazosin, prazosin and terazosin are named by the NHS as similar alpha blockers; NICE guidance lists alfuzosin, doxazosin, tamsulosin and terazosin as options for men's urinary symptoms.
